articles.title: CT Scans of Rare Dodo Skulls Uncover a Sensory World We Never Knew
articles.summary: High-res scans of the only two complete dodo skulls reveal the extinct bird likely had a keen sense of smell, a touch-sensitive beak, and may have been active at twilight. The findings challenge the old 'dumb dodo' myth.

articles.title: Engraved Ostrich Eggshells Reveal Early Humans' Geometric Mindset
articles.summary: A new analysis of 60,000-year-old engraved ostrich eggshells from southern Africa shows that over 80% of the markings follow geometric principles like parallelism and right angles. This suggests early Homo sapiens possessed advanced abstract thinking.

articles.title: World's First Air-Breathing Satellite Thruster Set for Orbital Test
articles.summary: Spanish startup Kreios Space is preparing to launch a satellite that uses air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) to operate in very low Earth orbit. The technology scoops up atmospheric air, ionizes it, and expels it as thrust, eliminating the need for onboard fuel.
